lines: [warm] Here's how to get JobFlow running in about five minutes, from the terminal.

lines.text: You need Node 20 or newer, and pnpm.
lines.say: You need Node twenty or newer, and p-n-p-m.

lines: Clone the repository, install the dependencies, and build. No account, no server, and no API key.

lines.text: Next, your profile. jobflow init reads your résumé and asks you to confirm what it found.
lines.say: Next, your profile. jobflow in-it reads your résumé, and asks you to confirm what it found.

lines.text: To look around first, init --sample loads a fictional candidate. That's what we'll use here.
lines.say: To look around first, in-it, dash dash sample, loads a fictional candidate. That's what we'll use here.

lines: jobflow sync checks the job boards in your discovery preset, with live progress: the step it's on, boards checked, jobs fetched, and time left.
[calm] This is demo mode, so the boards are fictional. When one doesn't answer, the summary says so, and it's tried again next sync.
jobflow feed is your ranked list. Each row has a score, the pay if it's known, and a line on why it fits.
Caveats, like a post from a staffing agency, get a line of their own.
jobflow show opens one job in full: how you fit, what to check, and an apply checklist with a fix for each gap.
When you'd rather use a browser, jobflow serve opens the web app on the same data, on your machine only.
[warm] From here, try jobflow search, tailor a résumé, and read the applying guide. Everything is in the docs folder.
